name: ACL2
note: untyped applicative Common Lisp with automated first-order theorem proving
typeSystem: Untyped, first-order, side-effect-free (applicative) subset of Common Lisp: every value is ordinary Lisp data (conses, symbols, numbers, strings), checked only at run time, with no separate static type layer.
runtime: Runs as a read-eval-print loop hosted inside a full Common Lisp implementation; ACL2 functions are ordinary (compiled) Lisp functions, so the theorem prover and the executable logic share the same evaluator.

runtimes.name: SBCL (host)
runtimes.role: Supported Common Lisp host; compiled ACL2 definitions can run as native machine code for fast execution and proof checking.

runtimes.name: CCL (host)
runtimes.role: Supported native-code Common Lisp host, and the recommended host for the experimental ACL2(p) parallel extension.

compilers.name: certify-book
compilers.role: Certifies libraries ('books') of ACL2 definitions and proved theorems so they can be trusted and reused without re-proving.

concurrencyModel: Standard ACL2's applicative logic has no built-in concurrency constructs. The experimental ACL2(p) extension supports parallel execution and proof, and host Lisps may provide threads outside the logic.

codeExample.caption: A recursive definition with a proved theorem about it
codeExample.source:
(defun fact (n)
  (if (zp n)
      1
      (* n (fact (1- n)))))

(defthm fact-positive
  (implies (natp n) (> (fact n) 0)))
